en.name: Nativity of Saint John the Baptist
en.summary: One of the very few birth celebrations in the Church calendar, marking the forerunner's arrival six months before Christ's.
en.body: The Church calendar generally commemorates saints on the date of their death, understood as their birth into eternal life, but it makes a small number of exceptions for figures whose earthly birth itself carried special theological significance, and John the Baptist's is one of only three such birth feasts alongside those of Jesus and Mary. Set six months before Christmas, in keeping with the Gospel of Luke's account that Elizabeth was already six months pregnant when Mary conceived, the feast celebrates John's identity as the forerunner of Christ, the one who, according to tradition, leapt in his mother's womb at Mary's approach. The feast has long been associated in European folk tradition with midsummer bonfires and celebrations tied to the summer solstice.
